1.why: All seven screens show a static, minimal single-column layout with no moving images, animations, or pop-up dialogs.

2.why: Primary buttons, bold headings, and teal status banners stand out clearly, though the large dark Logs panel with long hex tokens visually competes and buries the codes in dense text.

3.why: Each step offers one clearly labeled input and action that are easy to locate, but the 64-character recovery code must be found and transcribed from deep inside the Logs panel.

4.why: The five-step pill indicator keeps all steps visible so nothing must be memorized, and password rules are listed on-screen, though the rule set (12+ characters, upper/lowercase, number, symbol) is itself a fair amount to process.

5.why: No 'remember me' checkbox, password-manager option, or autofill affordance is visible on any screen—only plain input fields appear.

6.why: Persistent step pills, status banners ('Password saved…', 'Identity confirmed…'), and the Logs history let the user recognize prior actions and current state instead of recalling them.

7.why: Instructions are short and plain ('Enter your account email'), but some phrasing such as 'simulated recovery delivery' and 'whether or not an account matches' is technical.

8.why: No error message appears in any of the seven screenshots, so whether errors describe problems and fixes cannot be verified.

9.why: The Logs panel displays the actual codes to enter and step 2 points to the recovery link, but no example entries (e.g., sample email or example password) are given for other fields.

10.why: The flow offers one fixed path (email → code → password → sign-in → MFA) with no choice among login methods such as face login; the few in-step choices (verify vs. resend code) are clearly labeled.

11.why: Every screen presents at most one input field and one or two buttons, so the user never faces many choices at once.

12.why: Each action triggers an explicit outcome banner—'Code verified', 'Password saved', 'Identity confirmed. You are signed in', 'Privacy statement accepted'.

13.why: Every step includes a short tip banner (e.g., 'Take your time: this step will stay here until you are ready') plus a persistent 'Need help?' link.

14.why: A 'Send a new recovery code' button, the absence of any session countdown, and 'gently limited' resend requests support easy retries, though recovery from incorrect entries is not shown.

15.why: Header, step pills, banner style, button styling, help link, and Logs panel remain visually identical across all seven steps.
